quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

35 Questions • Passing Score 30

questions.question: When two vehicles arrive at a four-way stop at the same time, what should happen?

options.text: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
The vehicle on the right must yield to the vehicle on the left.
Drivers must use hand signals to communicate with each other.
One driver should proceed without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.
questions.explanation: At a four-way stop, vehicles proceed in the order they arrive. If two vehicles arrive at the same time, the vehicle on the left must yield to the vehicle on the right.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Road conditions greatly affect how quickly you can stop. On slippery or poor roads, you need to slow down to maintain control and stop safely.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the roadway?

options.text: Pass the animal as closely as possible.

questions.explanation: Be very cautious when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
Two lanes of traffic are about to merge in opposite directions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The overpass ahead has low clearance.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the overpass ahead has low clearance. Do not proceed if your vehicle is taller than the height shown on the sign (for example, 13 feet 6 inches).

questions.question: Why is it important to leave space between your vehicle and others?

options.text: It prevents distractions from other vehicles.
It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
It keeps traffic moving at a safe speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It gives you time to react to unexpected situations.
questions.explanation: Leave plenty of space between you and other vehicles. This gives you time to react if other drivers make mistakes.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Be ready to stop for a yellow or red light.

questions.question: When a traffic light turns green, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up as quickly as possible.
Wait for another driver to wave you on.

questions.explanation: A green light means you can go, but you must first let any traffic and pedestrians still in the intersection pass safely.

questions.question: What should you do if there is an oncoming car to your left and a bicyclist to your right?

options.text: Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let the car pass, then pass the bicyclist.
questions.explanation: Handle one hazard at a time. Let the oncoming car pass first, then pass the bicyclist. Do not try to squeeze between both at the same time.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?
questions.explanation: This sign means a divided highway is starting ahead. The road will split into two separate one-way roads. Stay to the right.

questions.question: When must you yield for emergency vehicles?

options.text: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see flashing red or blue lights or hear a siren.
questions.explanation: Always yield the right-of-way to emergency vehicles using sirens or flashing lights.

questions.question: An inattentive driver is someone who:

options.text: Looks at objects off the road or daydreams while driving.
Makes eye contact with a passenger while driving.
Only watches the car directly ahead.

questions.explanation: Do not look at passengers, search for items in your car, read, look at scenery, or daydream while driving. Keep scanning the road. Check your mirrors and instrument panel regularly. These safe habits keep you focused on driving.

questions.question: If another car is about to hit you, you should:
questions.explanation: Use your horn to warn other drivers or pedestrians who may not see you. For example, sound your horn if you think another driver is about to hit you.

questions.question: A single broken white line down the center of a two-lane road means:

options.text: Lanes go in opposite directions. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes go in opposite directions. Drivers can pass when safe.
Lanes go in the same direction. Drivers cannot pass.
Lanes go in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Lanes go in the same direction. Drivers can pass when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. A dashed white line means drivers next to it can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: The speed limit in school zones is:
questions.explanation: Unless posted differently, the speed limit in school zones, residential areas, and business zones is 25 mph for cars and motorcycles. Pay attention to when the school zone speed limit applies.

questions.question: This road sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a traffic signal is coming. Slow down and be ready to stop.

questions.question: What should you do if your vehicle's right wheels leave the pavement?

options.text: Pull all the way off the road immediately and return when safe.
Speed up and steer back onto the road quickly.
Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the accelerator, slow down, then carefully steer back onto the road when safe.
questions.explanation: If your right wheels leave the pavement, stay calm. Release the accelerator and steer parallel to the road. Slow down and ease back onto the road by keeping both hands on the wheel and making a small turn. Check for traffic before steering back onto the pavement.

questions.question: When approaching a road construction or maintenance area:

options.text: Keep your vehicle in the middle of the lane and follow the speed limit.
Watch for flashing arrow signs, message boards, construction signs, and flaggers.

questions.explanation: In a work zone, drive near the middle of your lane and obey the posted speed limit. Do not change lanes until you have completely passed the work zone. Flashing arrow signs, message boards, construction signs, and flaggers may give you special instructions.

questions.question: Double solid yellow lines mean you may pass another vehicle from either direction.
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means drivers in both directions cannot cross the center line to pass.

questions.question: Smoking and preparing to smoke while driving:

options.text: Help keep you alert while driving.

questions.explanation: Smoking while driving is a dangerous distraction. It takes your hands off the wheel and your eyes off the road.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Do not speed on wet roads.
Keep your tires at the correct air pressure.

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning occurs when your vehicle slides on a thin layer of water between the tires and road. Low tire pressure and worn tread increase hydroplaning risk. Speeding on wet roads also increases this risk.

questions.question: Don't follow other cars too closely because:

options.text: You may not see the road between the cars.
You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
You may not see the turn signals.
You may not see the brake lights.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may not have time to stop if the car in front stops suddenly.
questions.explanation: If you follow too closely and the car in front stops suddenly, you may not have enough time to stop and could crash.

questions.question: Compared to driving during the day, driving at night is:
questions.explanation: Night driving is more dangerous because it is harder to see, headlights can blind you, and more tired or impaired drivers may be on the road.

questions.question: When two cars enter an intersection at the same time, which one must yield?
questions.explanation: When two cars arrive at an intersection at the same time, the car on the left must yield to the car on the right.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings and diamond-shaped. This sign warns you that a steep hill is coming. Slow down and be ready to adjust your speed.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
The road has sharp turns or curves ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: Reduce your speed when the road is wet.
questions.explanation: This sign warns that the road is slippery when wet. Slow down, avoid sudden braking or turns, and stay farther from the car ahead.

questions.question: This road sign shows:

options.text: The safe speed for a residential area.
The safe speed for an expressway exit.
The safe speed for an expressway entrance.
The safe speed for a work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The safe speed for an expressway exit.
questions.explanation: This sign shows the recommended safe speed for exiting a highway, such as 30 mph in this example.

questions.question: This sign means:
questions.explanation: This sign warns that bicycles may be on or near the road ahead.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Stop and look for police cars.

questions.explanation: You may turn right on a green light unless a sign says not to. When you turn, you must let other cars and pedestrians in the intersection go first.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The traffic light ahead is red.
The traffic light ahead is broken.
The traffic light ahead is green.

questions.explanation: This sign warns that a traffic light is at the next intersection.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs mean:
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs tell you that a train crossing is ahead. Yield to trains and do not try to drive around the gates.

questions.question: If a green arrow turns into a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You may turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
You must go straight and cannot turn.
You have the right-of-way to turn.
You do not have to turn in the direction the arrow showed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow becomes a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. However, you must first yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: At night, how should you look to avoid bright headlight glare?

options.text: At the center of the road.
To the right edge of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: To the right edge of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look at the right side of the road ahead. Do not look directly at the bright headlights, as the glare can blind you for several seconds.

questions.question: Your tire blows out while driving. What should you do?

options.text: Grip the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
Turn on flashers and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Grip the steering wheel firmly and slow down gradually.
questions.explanation: If a tire blows out, do not brake hard right away. Hold the steering wheel tightly to stay in your lane. Slowly release the accelerator to reduce speed. Once you are going very slowly, apply the brakes gently and pull safely off the road.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Construction workers on or near the road.

questions.explanation: Warning signs are diamond-shaped with black markings on a yellow background. They warn drivers about hazards ahead. This sign tells drivers that people may be crossing the road.

questions.question: When you approach a railroad crossing with no flashing lights or gates, what should you do?

options.text: Be ready to yield to any train.
Speed up to cross before a train arrives.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to any train.
questions.explanation: Always be ready to yield to trains at railroad crossings, especially when there are no lights or gates. Only cross when your entire vehicle can fit safely on the other side. Do not shift gears while crossing, as your vehicle might stall.
